The default policy fills in arrival order from one shared counter, so 256 slots went to ~26 layers of position 0 and measured **2.97%**.  Per-layer, the same routing gives 21.4% at 8 slots/layer and 70.4% at 64.

no host arena: experts read from the GGUF on demand (needs a native pack and a VRAM cache that holds every expert; for machines with less RAM than experts) The A/B arm: the mmap's rate depends on the OS page cache holding 34 GB, and measured 71.97 vs 34.78 ms/token cold vs warm.
Linux: back the resident arena with one MAP_SHARED file. Put this file on /dev/shm, not ordinary SSD storage. A small header binds an existing backing file to the same pack.

with mmap and a static profile, keep the experts the GPU cache does not hold resident in ordinary RAM (and the prompt path's lend region as far as RAM allows); adaptive swaps exchange them, so none is read from the file again.

the low-RAM PC's resident mode (setup): --mmap-experts --resident-cpu-experts with the copy page-locked when possible, 4 GiB headroom, plain mmap if it does not fit.  Same answers as --mmap-experts for the same placement.

prompt path must not lend expert slots (long prompts hang without it)
VRAM kept free; the engine sizes its expert cache off this

the draft head's token subset (setup's --draft-vocab). LAUNCHER-APPLIED: copies data/draft_vocab_<x>.bin over mtp/rt/draft_vocab.bin just before start. The engine itself takes no such flag, so it is never put on the command line. The head is sized by that file (4-byte token ids): the cjk default is 106,299 ids, en is 40,525 (137.9 -> 52.6 MiB measured on IQ2_XS, 81.2 MiB for the same en subset on the Coder), and what it frees goes to the reserve/expert slots. rt/ is shared by every model.

the system-prompt checkpoint: a prompt read from the start is checkpointed at the end of its system prompt when that is N tokens or more (docs say the default threshold is 2,048; 0 = no system-prompt checkpoint). Not in the engine's --help, which is why it is marked undocumented - the built binary accepts it (checked with strings).
